title: Quantum computation of partonic Drell-Yan scattering cross sections and interference effects
authors: Erik Bashore, Stefano Moretti, Timea Vitos
abstract: We probe the possibilities of efficiently constructing simple Feynman diagrams into quantum devices. More precisely, we study Drell-Yan lepton pair creation at the partonic level of the form q qbar -> gamma/Z -> l- l+. We develop quantum gates that build up the relevant diagrams using simple Feynman rules, such as vertex and propagator gates V and P. We show how the quantum circuit may compute simultaneous amplitudes in the phase space and how to reach the full integrated cross section from the outputs. In addition to this, we also show how the circuit is able to simultaneously isolate the interference effects of the contributing diagrams by a simple basis rotation. The circuit design is made to be general, and thus this work constitutes a step towards the implementation of arbitrary scattering process computations and efficient interference analyses.
summary: This work proposes using quantum computation to calculate scattering cross sections for processes like Drell-Yan scattering by encoding Feynman diagrams into quantum gates. The authors develop a general circuit that can simultaneously compute the total cross-section and isolate interference effects by leveraging quantum superposition over phase space coordinates.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently calculating complex scattering cross sections, particularly including interference effects, by mapping Feynman diagram calculations onto quantum circuits.
main_result: They demonstrate a general quantum circuit design capable of simultaneously estimating the full integrated cross-section and isolating interference terms for processes like Drell-Yan scattering.
method: The methodology involves constructing specialized quantum gates (Vertex, Propagator, Spinor) that encode Feynman rules, and then using quantum superposition and basis rotations to evaluate phase space integrals and interference terms.
model_or_system: The physical system is the partonic Drell-Yan lepton pair creation process ($q ar{q} ightarrow \gamma/Z ightarrow \ell^-\ell^+$) within the Standard Model electroweak theory. The computation is performed using quantum circuits simulating the underlying quantum field theory interactions.
key_observables: Full integrated cross-section ($\sigma$) and the isolated interference contribution ($	ext{Int} \langle M_i, M_j angle$).
important_parameters: The process depends on the interplay between photon ($\gamma$) and $Z$ boson contributions, and the calculation requires discretizing the phase space over energy ($\sqrt{s}$) and scattering angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The initial focus is restricted to the partonic level, neglecting Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs). Furthermore, unitarity requires defining a 'pole factor roof' $ ar{m}$ for rescaling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the decomposition of fundamental gates (Dirac matrices, $\eta$ gate, spinor gates, Vertex, Propagator) and show the full quantum circuit for the DY process, including PS control registers $E$ and $\Theta$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically details the construction of necessary quantum gates (Dirac matrices, metric, spinor states, vertices, propagators) into fundamental quantum gates, followed by demonstrating the full circuit for the DY process, and finally showing how PS integration and interference isolation are achieved.
why_interesting: While focused on particle physics, the core contribution is the development of a general, scalable quantum circuit framework for simulating complex quantum field theory amplitudes, which is a major computational primitive for quantum algorithms.
